source.title: Neural Network Weights Do Not Converge to Stationary Points: An Invariant Measure Perspective
source.authors: J. Zhang; Haochuan Li; Suvrit Sra; A. Jadbabaie

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The supplied text includes flattened figure content and some apparent transcription errors, but the relevant prose and appendix are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports gradient-based training results that refine the broad claim: large ImageNet and WT103 runs can stabilize training loss without converging to stationary points, while its CIFAR-10 experiment reports the gradient norm converging to zero. Its measured outcomes concern gradient norm and loss stabilization, not training classification error, so they do not directly test the specified V1–V6 behaviors.
record.gate_note: The paper measures training loss, gradient norm, stochastic-gradient noise, and sharpness during training. It does not report training classification error, label corruption, or the bad-local-minimum, shortcut, initialization, learning-rate-stability, or batch-normalization comparisons specified by V1–V6. The CIFAR-10 result is retained because the paper explicitly reports that the gradient norm converges to zero; this is relevant to the claim's subject but does not establish near-zero training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study measures loss stabilization, gradient norms and training dynamics, but does not test any specified version. Stationarity is distinct from training classification error; its learning-rate experiments do not establish stability-threshold tracking, catapult recovery or divergence relative to that threshold. Section 5.1 offers a speculative connection to edge of stability rather than a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's empirical paraphrase is accurate: loss can stabilize without gradient norms vanishing in the large-scale runs, while CIFAR-10 is an exception. The theoretical conclusion needs precision: the authors establish vanishing time-averaged expected loss change under assumptions and develop an approximate invariant-measure perspective. They do not establish low loss, optimality, generalization, or general convergence of the entire empirical-measure sequence; they explicitly allow failure of a time-average limit.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies convergence of training loss and gradient norms during practical SGD training and develops an invariant-measure analysis. It does not apply the original claim's training-classification-error outcome or its specified interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies across task/scale: ImageNet with ResNet101 and WT103 with Transformer-XL show nonzero gradient norms while CIFAR-10 with ResNet shows the gradient norm converging to zero. The paper also varies learning-rate schedule and rate for ImageNet and WT103.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet ResNet101 and WT103 Transformer-XL runs retain nonzero gradient norms despite stabilizing loss; the extended ImageNet run does not resolve this. CIFAR-10 ResNet instead shows gradient norm approaching zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss stabilization need not imply convergence to stationary points, with behavior differing across the tested tasks and models.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient descent on the sinusoidal objective reaches a stationary point at learning rate 0.01 and oscillates at 0.04, with convergent time averages in the illustrated trajectory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The studied analytic objective permits oscillatory dynamics with stable time averages above its smoothness-based step-size bound.

fits_no_version.finding: Averaging minibatch losses across updates produces a smoother curve than evaluating the whole dataset at an epoch's final weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent training-loss stabilization depends on the temporal averaging used to measure loss.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: The central large-scale trajectories are primarily shown in figures, without numerical effect sizes or uncertainty estimates. Statistics are estimated from random batches smaller than the full dataset; the authors note that estimated ImageNet sharpness varies greatly. The paper explicitly says its analysis proves vanishing change in average training loss, not the actual loss values, local or global optimality, or generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No required results omitted. The four Transformer-XL schedule/rate settings are retained as separate rows, but the prose does not assign separate numeric outcomes to each; no precise values are reconstructed from Figure 3.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their frequency under extra student width.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons establishing faster learning, preserved signal propagation or greater trainable depth.
Catapult recovery and divergence relative to initial linearized stability limits; full-batch sharpness tracking the stability threshold while loss decreases; divergence from below the threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance, and equivalent training performance using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are assessed against V1–V6. A cannot_determine state here does not dispute the reported off-version finding. The prose's negative association between sharpness and learning rate supplies no measured stability-threshold trajectory, and its batch-normalization theorem supplies no training-speed comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification outcomes, random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size or early stopping are not reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum frequency, or student-width comparison.
No depth comparison of plain and residual networks, and no training-error comparison for identity shortcuts, deep tanh networks, or normalization-free residual networks.
No initialization comparison, signal or gradient propagation measurement across depth, or initialization-based trainable-depth comparison.
No test of learning rates above a stability limit, curvature drop or threshold tracking, or divergence relative to that limit.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison of accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and no Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet101
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, gradient norm, stochastic-gradient noise and validation top-1 accuracy during ImageNet training using the standard stage-wise schedule.

conditions.value: learning rate starts at 0.1 and is decayed by a factor of 10 every 30 epochs

rows.measure: Training loss, gradient norm and stochastic-gradient noise over training; validation top-1 accuracy also plotted.
rows.value: Within each period where the step size is held constant, the change in loss converges to 0; the gradient norm does not converge to 0 and stays roughly unchanged; noise level increases during training.
rows.note: No training classification error is reported; the paper describes plotted curves and summarizes their behavior in text.
rows.check: The reported loss and gradient behavior is supported, but these measures cannot establish any version's effect.

rows.subject: ResNet101
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, gradient norm, noise and sharpness while training with a constant learning rate.
rows.measure: Training loss, gradient norm, noise and sharpness over epochs.
rows.value: The text says the gradient norm does not converge to 0 in any of the constant-learning-rate experiments; figure-only curves are shown for this setting.
rows.note: No training classification error is reported.
rows.check: Nonzero gradient norm does not test a version. Figure 2 plots loss, gradient norm and noise, not sharpness; remove sharpness from the operation and measure.

rows.subject: ResNet101
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, gradient norm, noise and sharpness during an extended constant-learning-rate run.
rows.measure: Training loss and gradient norm over epochs.
rows.value: After about 50 epochs, no clear progress was made; after 300 epochs, training loss had dropped significantly but gradient norm did not decrease.
rows.note: The text explicitly says that longer training did not make the gradient norm decrease; it does not report classification error.
rows.check: Longer training without decreasing gradient norm does not establish training classification error or a V5 stability-threshold result. Figure 2 does not plot sharpness; remove it from the operation.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, gradient norm and noise during CIFAR-10 training.

conditions.value: learning rate starts at 0.1 and decays by a factor of 10 at epoch 100 and epoch 150

rows.value: The authors report that the gradient norm converges to 0.
rows.note: This is a CIFAR-10 gradient-norm result, not a training classification-error measurement.
rows.check: Gradient norm approaching zero on CIFAR-10 does not establish near-zero training classification error. The authors' description of overfitting supplies no classification-error measurement.

rows.subject: Synthetic gradient-descent trajectory
rows.operation_detail: Compared gradient descent trajectories at two learning rates on f(θ1, θ2) = 100 sin θ1 sin θ2.

conditions.value: f(θ1, θ2) = 100 sin θ1 sin θ2

rows.measure: Trajectory, training loss and gradient norm.
rows.value: Iterates converge to a fixed point quickly and the gradient norm converges to zero.
rows.note: Toy smooth objective, not a neural network benchmark.
rows.check: This is a two-variable analytic objective, not a toy neural network. Its fixed-point convergence does not test any version.

rows.subject: Synthetic gradient-descent trajectory
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient descent trajectory at a learning rate above 2/Lf.

conditions.value: f(θ1, θ2) = 100 sin θ1 sin θ2

rows.measure: Trajectory, training loss and gradient norm.
rows.value: Iterates oscillate among a few points and training loss and gradient norm oscillate rather than converge in the usual sense; their time averages converge, with average gradient norm not zero.
rows.note: Toy smooth objective, not a neural network benchmark.
rows.check: This is an analytic objective, not a neural network. Oscillation above its global smoothness bound does not test V5's neural-network catapult or edge-of-stability behavior.

rows.subject: ResNet101
rows.operation_detail: Compared the usual moving-average training loss over minibatches with full-batch loss evaluated at the last iteration of each epoch.
rows.measure: Training loss evaluated as a moving average during an epoch versus at the last iteration.
rows.value: The moving-average loss curve is described as much smoother than the fixed-iteration full-batch loss curve.
rows.note: The authors offer time averaging as one possible explanation; the row records the stated comparison.
rows.check: The loss-averaging comparison is supported but does not measure any version's effect.
